rows.explanation: It identifies the saints by patience, obedience to God's commandments, and faith in Jesus, closely paralleling belief, righteous action, and perseverance.
It commends works, love, service, faith, and patience together, closely echoing the linked qualities in the ayah.
It describes people who keep the heard word and bear fruit with patience, joining truth received, faithful action, and endurance.
It asks whether claimed faith without works can save, making faith joined to deeds decisive against loss.
It calls faith without works dead, matching the ayah's union of belief and righteous deeds.
It says faith worked together with works and was completed by them, directly joining belief and action.
It compares faith without works to a dead body, sharply affirming that faith must have active expression.
It rejects professed fellowship with God that walks in darkness as a lie and a failure to do the truth.
It promises eternal life to those who persist patiently in doing good.
It contrasts mere hearers with doers of God's law who are justified, paralleling true adherence joined to action.
It says that the promises are inherited through faith and patience.
It joins patience and doing God's will with receiving the promise.
It exhorts disciples to continue in faith through tribulation in order to enter God's kingdom.
It joins persistence in sound teaching with salvation for both the teacher and those who hear.
It commands exhortation grounded in the word and doctrine with all longsuffering.
It calls the brethren to warn, comfort, support, and be patient toward all.
It joins obedience to truth with fervent reciprocal love among believers.
It commands love in deed and truth rather than merely in word.
It promises reaping to those who do good without becoming weary.
It makes salvation depend on holding fast the preached message rather than having believed in vain.
It calls believers to steadfastness and abundant work because their labor is not vain.
It excludes mere profession and admits into the kingdom those who do the Father's will.
It makes sharing in Christ conditional on holding initial confidence steadfast to the end.
It directs sufferers to entrust themselves to God while continuing in well-doing.
It commends works, labor, patience, and discerning false apostles as liars.
It joins loving, obeying, and cleaving to God with life itself.
It joins continual meditation on God's instruction with doing it and receiving success.
It joins knowing, serving, and seeking God with being found by him rather than cast off.
It directly pairs trusting the LORD with doing good and receiving his provision.
It commands turning to God, keeping justice, and waiting on God continually.
It joins seeking God's law, doing it, and teaching it to others.
It joins truth in speech, upright conduct, and turning many away from iniquity.
It commands mutual consideration that spurs love and good works.
It joins goodness and knowledge with the ability to admonish one another.
It counts the faith of one who does not work as righteousness, opposing a reading in which righteous deeds are required for rescue from loss.
It says salvation is not by righteous works done by people but by mercy, answering the ayah's deeds condition in the opposite causal direction.
It says salvation is not of works, opposing works as a condition or basis for escaping loss.
It says God saved and called believers not according to works but according to grace.
It concludes that a person is justified by faith without deeds of the law.
It denies justification by works of the law and locates it in faith in Christ.
It rejects one's own righteousness from the law in favor of righteousness through faith in Christ.
It portrays people demanding deceitful rather than right prophecy, reversing exhortation toward truth.
It commands believers to exhort one another as the day approaches.
It commands believers to teach and admonish one another with Christ's word.
It joins holding the faithful word with exhorting others by sound doctrine.
It commands each person to speak truth with his neighbor as fellow members.
It commands truthful speech to one's neighbor together with judgments of truth and peace.
It requires direct brotherly rebuke rather than allowing sin to remain unaddressed.
It treats a friend's painful correction as faithful and deceptive affection as false.
It commands private correction of a sinning brother in order to gain him back.
It promises salvation to the person who endures to the end.
It promises salvation to the person who endures to the end amid hatred.
It connects patience with preserving one's life.
It makes continuing in Jesus's word the mark of those who had believed in him.
It describes faith as working through love.
It calls believers to stand fast and strive together for the faith of the gospel.
It commands mutual forbearance and forgiveness, supplying the ayah's communal patience.
It commends patience and faith amid persecutions and tribulations endured.
It tells believers not to grow weary in doing good.
It says those who have believed in God should be careful to maintain good works.
It commands daily mutual exhortation so that none is hardened by sin's deceitfulness.
It calls believers to hold fast their profession of faith without wavering.
It says the testing of faith produces patience.
It commands hearers of the word to become doers rather than deceive themselves.
It commands patience and steadfast hearts in view of the Lord's coming.
It directs believers to add virtue to faith through deliberate moral growth.
It explicitly includes patience in the same faith-based moral progression.
It adds brotherly kindness and love to that progression's ethical character.
It identifies God's children by practicing righteousness and loving fellow believers.
It joins faith in Jesus with the command to love one another.
It promises protection to those who have kept Christ's word of patience.
It names patience and faith as the defining response of the saints.
It joins commanding God's way, doing justice, and receiving God's promised blessing.
It links Ruth's work and her trust in Israel's God with a hoped-for divine reward.
It joins walking in God's statutes and commandments with prospering under his care.
It exhorts courage and continued work on the promise that the work will be rewarded.
It records prophetic calls to turn from evil and keep God's commandments.
It says the righteous hold on to their way and grow stronger in clean-handedness.
It describes the acceptable person as one who works righteousness and speaks truth inwardly.
It commands encouragement to fearful hearts with the assurance that God will come and save.
It calls it good to hope quietly and wait for the LORD's salvation.
It promises life to the person who walks in God's statutes and does what is lawful and right.
It promises lasting glory to those who turn many toward righteousness.
It commands waiting for the sure fulfillment of God's apparently delayed vision.
It contrasts the proud with the righteous person who lives by faith.
It joins seeking the LORD, righteousness, and humility with possible shelter from wrath.
It commands true judgment and merciful treatment of one another.
It tells hearers to wait on the LORD and keep his way, promising inheritance while the wicked are cut off.
It explicitly joins hope for God's salvation with doing his commandments.
It calls for sowing righteousness, seeking the LORD, and receiving his merciful righteousness.
It rejects calling Jesus Lord without doing what he says, matching the demand that belief be enacted.
It calls the persistent hearer a doer and promises that he will be blessed in his deed.
It says all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
It says Israel failed because it pursued righteousness as from works rather than from faith.
It contrasts receiving the Spirit through hearing with faith against receiving it through works of the law.
It joins teaching God's ordinances with showing people the way to walk and the work to do.
It contrasts the LORD-known way of the righteous with the perishing way of the wicked.
It commands fearing and serving the LORD in truth with the whole heart.
It warns that persisting in wickedness brings consumption, reinforcing loss outside faithful righteousness.
It promises a sure reward to the person who sows righteousness.
It describes the secure righteous person through upright walking and truthful speech.
It portrays those who wait on the LORD as receiving strength to continue without weariness.
It depicts neighbors helping one another and urging their brothers to courage.
It makes warning the wicked to turn from his way a life-and-death moral exhortation.
It promises life to the wicked person who turns to restitution and walks in statutes of life.
It commands seeking good rather than evil so that people may live with the LORD.
It promises salvation to the person who endures to the end.
It commands rebuking a sinning brother and forgiving him when he repents.
It calls spiritual believers to restore an erring person gently while guarding themselves.
It commands longsuffering and mutual forbearance in love.
It joins goodness, righteousness, and truth as the fruit of the Spirit.
It joins holding forth the word of life with labor that is not vain at Christ's day.
It calls believers to fruitful good works while increasing in knowledge of God.
It connects divine strength with all patience and longsuffering.
It makes continuing grounded and steadfast in faith the condition of remaining in gospel hope.
It joins unfeigned faith with love from a pure heart and good conscience.
It joins righteousness, faith, love, and patience as virtues to pursue.
It links suffering endurance with reigning with Christ and denial of him with his denial.
It calls for soundness in faith, love, and patience.
It describes Christ's people as purified and zealous for good works.
It calls the enduring person blessed and promises a crown of life after testing.
It uses the farmer's waiting for precious fruit as an image of patient endurance.
It presents the prophets as examples of suffering and patience.
It calls those who endure blessed and invokes Job's patience.
It commands steadfast resistance in faith amid sufferings shared by fellow believers.
It calls for diligence to make one's calling sure and promises no fall when these virtues are practiced.
It makes keeping God's commandments the evidence of knowing him.
It defines love for God as keeping his commandments.
It commands faithfulness unto death and promises the crown of life.
It identifies the faithful remnant by keeping God's commandments and holding Jesus's testimony.
It describes people turning their ears away from truth and turning instead to fables.
It depicts false prophecy and a people who welcome it, reversing communal commitment to truth.
